titleText.es: Al principio no te creíamos, pero le preguntamos a unas tres personas que estuvieron en esa fiesta. No solo corroboraron tu historia, sino que además dijeron que mencionaste que querías montar una empresa algún día. ¡Lo sentimos! Si esto no es suficiente dinero, dínoslo.
titleText.en: We didn't believe you at first, but we asked like three people who were at that party. They not only corroborated your story, but even said you totally mentioned wanting to start a company someday. Sorry! If this isn't enough money, let us know.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and English texts are the exact title attributes from the Spanish archive and official xkcd. OCR omitted most small form text and the right-hand button and delivery panel, split SOLICITAN-/DO, lost several accents and initial letters, and fused several form labels. The monetary amount, percentages, address, English button label, personal name, and delivery-company logo are audited exclusions. Cursor art, form borders, browser controls, hand pointer, dollar markings, figures, furniture, and speech tails are structural artwork.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Empresa is a feminine noun for a company or business organization.

example.es: La empresa abrió una oficina pequeña.
example.en: The company opened a small office.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hecho is the irregular completed-action form of hacer. With se and a form of haber, it helps form hacerse + description, meaning to become or grow into a new state. After haber, hecho does not change to match a feminine or plural subject.

example.es: El barrio se ha hecho famoso.
example.en: The neighborhood has become famous.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Parte can mean one portion of a whole. In money or ownership contexts, it can be the share that belongs to a person.

example.es: Cada socio recibió su parte de las ganancias.
example.en: Each partner received their share of the profits.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: that (fixed linker in claro que sí)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In claro que sí, que links claro to the emphatic sí. Learn the three words together as a common expression of confident agreement.

example.en: 'Will you come tomorrow?' 'Of course.'

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Solicitando is the -ando form of solicitar. It presents a formal request or application as an ongoing action.

example.en: I am applying for a scholarship.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A departamento can be a division within an organization. In some countries it can also mean an apartment or an administrative region.

example.es: Envía el formulario al departamento correcto.
example.en: Send the form to the correct department.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fecha is the calendar date associated with an event or document.

example.es: Escribe la fecha en la primera línea.
example.en: Write the date on the first line.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tuviste is the informal singular completed-past form of tener. It refers to something one person had at a finished time.

example.en: Did you have time yesterday?

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Prueba can mean a test, but it also means information or material that supports a claim.

example.es: Necesitamos una prueba de que ocurrió.
example.en: We need proof that it happened.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; introducing what the evidence proves
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After prueba, de can introduce the content supported by the evidence. When a whole statement follows, Spanish uses de que.

example.es: Hay pruebas de que el plan funciona.
example.en: There is evidence that the plan works.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Preguntarle combines preguntar with attached le. The unchanged dictionary form names the action, while le identifies one person being asked.

example.en: You can ask the neighbor.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: in (fixed part of estar en plan)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En belongs to the colloquial expression estar en plan. The expression presents someone's attitude, mode, or approximate words.

example.en: She was in an optimistic sort of mood.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: mode; like (fixed part of estar en plan)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In colloquial estar en plan, plan does not mean a literal plan. It helps frame an attitude, manner, or loose quotation.

example.en: He was like, 'It's no big deal.'

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Respondió is the third-person singular completed-past form of responder.

example.en: The director replied immediately.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you; for yourself (small pronoun used with merecerse)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With informal singular tú, te is the matching small pronoun in merecerse algo. It appears before a form that matches the person and time, such as mereces.

example.en: You deserve a break.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mereces is the informal singular present form of merecer. In the common pronominal pattern, it appears as te mereces.

example.en: You deserve a clear answer.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sé is the irregular affirmative command of ser for one familiar listener. Its written accent distinguishes it from se.

example.en: Be patient with others.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Justo describes a masculine singular person, choice, or result that is fair or morally right.

example.en: We are seeking a fair agreement.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dirección can mean direction, management, or an address. With postal, it is the address used for mail.

example.es: Confirma tu dirección antes del envío.
example.en: Confirm your address before shipment.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you give a confident 'of course' answer to a yes-or-no question?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Claro que sí strongly confirms a positive answer. Claro que no gives the corresponding confident negative answer.

example.en: 'Will you help me?' 'Of course.'

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce the statement that some evidence supports?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use prueba de que, followed by the statement.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Prueba names the evidence, de links it to its content, and que introduces a complete idea with its own verb.

example.es: Esta foto es prueba de que llegaron temprano.
example.en: This photo is proof that they arrived early.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: estar en plan + actitud o palabras aproximadas
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can colloquial Spanish frame someone's attitude, manner, or loose quotation?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of estar followed by en plan, then give the attitude or approximate words.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This informal expression is especially common in Spain. It can describe a mood or work much like conversational English 'be like' before an approximate quotation.

example.en: We were in a relaxed sort of mood.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone deserves something, using the common pattern with me, te, se, nos, or os?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put the matching small pronoun before a form of merecer that matches the person and time, then name the deserved thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: For example, te mereces is used with tú and se merece with él, ella, or usted. The thing deserved can follow the verb or be understood from context.

example.en: You all deserve a vacation.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say mailing address or postal address?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Postal follows the feminine noun dirección but has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.

example.es: La solicitud pide una dirección postal.
example.en: The application asks for a mailing address.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: idea antigua · empresa rica · solicitar una parte · formulario retroactivo
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the business-idea department turn the speaker's complaint into a joke?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: It treats a vague old remark as if it were formal evidence that entitles someone to a retroactive share of a company's profits.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The speaker first makes the familiar claim that a company got rich from an idea he had years earlier. The next panels imagine an official form accepting hearsay, an approximate date, a self-selected percentage, and a mailing address, followed by an implausibly immediate cash delivery.

applications.explanationEn: Prueba names the evidence, de que introduces its content, and la tuviste supplies the complete claim being supported.
Se comes before lo: se refers to the person told, while lo stands for the thing that was said.

applications.exampleEs: SE LO DIJE A MI AMIGO
applications.explanationEn: The later phrase a mi amigo makes the person represented by se explicit; se is required instead of le before lo.
Puedes is the form of poder for one familiar listener, and preguntar stays in its unchanged dictionary form inside preguntarle, with le attached.
Le attaches to the end of the unchanged infinitive preguntar to identify one person being asked.
Estaba already identifies a first-person subject, so printed yo adds explicit focus before the quoted recollection.
Estaba sets a past state, and en plan colloquially frames the loose quotation that follows.
Neutral lo and relative que combine to refer to an unspecified idea or thing.
The ordinary statement-shaped frame sabes lo que sería remains in place; the surrounding question marks and intonation make it a yes-or-no question without an extra helper word.
Sería supplies the ‘would be’ form of ser for the imagined good idea.
Buena appears before idea because it gives an evaluation of the idea as a whole.
Buena uses feminine singular -a to agree with feminine singular idea.
Tuviste presents having the idea as a completed past event.
Dije presents telling the friend as a completed past event.
Estaba supplies an ongoing background state before the remembered quotation.
Respondió presents the reply as a completed past event.
